objective: Freeze a Boolean encoding exactly matching nonempty shores and possibly empty crossing matching, with manually composed resolution proof objects and positive boundary witnesses.

atomic_claims.text: For finite simple n>=1, the two nonempty-shore clauses and neighbour-pair clauses are satisfiable exactly when the frozen matching-cut predicate holds; fixing the first colour preserves satisfiability.
The package provides manually composed resolution contradictions for K1 and symmetry-reduced K(2,3), and four positive cut witnesses, with no checker execution claimed.
Cut satisfiability is separate from average/girth admissibility; rational strict average degree is tested by 2mq<pn, and K1 admissibility is uniform in real d>0 and integer g>=3.
Omitting nonempty-shore clauses wrongly accepts K1, while requiring a nonempty crossing set wrongly rejects the edgeless order-two graph.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs, vertices 1 through n with n>=1, and the frozen nonempty-shore, possibly-empty-matching convention.
Resolution clauses use signed integer literals; the proof objects are candidate data, not registered verifier receipts.
No external extremal or expander theorem is needed for this package.
risks: No solver, graph enumerator, proof assistant or proof-object checker was run; schema/hash/CI checks are transport only.
The certificate format needs separate checking of graph-to-formula reconstruction and inference steps.
ambiguous_problem_contract remains nonterminal; K1 is not silently excluded and both admitted obligations remain open.
Finite graph proof objects do not search the odd-order residual or supply general real-parameter computation.
